title: Colombo sees over 250 fire incidents so far this year
byline: A total of 258 fire incidents have been reported in Colombo and its surrounding areas during this year, the Fire Service Department has revealed.

title: Seek prompt medical treatment if children’s fever persists over 24 hours: Health authorities
byline: In the wake of growing risk of dengue spread, Health authorities urged parents to seek prompt medical treatment without delay, if children’s fever persists for more than 24 hours.

title: Oil market alarming for Sri Lanka, CPC seeks meeting with President
byline: With the global oil market remaining volatile due to tensions in the Middle East, the Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (CPC) has sought an urgent meeting with President Anura Kumara Dissanayake to discuss fresh measures to mitigate the impact, an official said.

title: Sajith denies political deal with BASL President
byline: Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa yesterday denied the allegation made by National People’s Power (NPP) MP Asitha Niroshana that Bar Association of Sri Lanka (BASL) President Rajiv Amarasuriya had got into a political deal with him.

title: Police OIC becomes hit and run driver
byline: A hit and run driver, allegedly a senior police official, who knocked down two young women at two locations and fled in his car was arrested by Meegoda Police yesterday.

title: Sri Lanka’s underworld violence escalates
byline: Sri Lanka has recorded 22 shooting incidents so far this year, leaving 15 people dead and 12 others injured. Nearly half of these incidents, 10 in total, were reported within the two-week period between July 11 and July 25.

title: Iran says it will halt strikes as long as US bombing pause holds
byline: Iran will halt its own attacks as long as the United States does the same, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Sunday. The development comes as the United States pressed pause on its bombing campaign after President Donald Trump’s advisers told him they were running out of targets and expressed worries about depleting the U.S. arsenal.

title: Oil prices plunge 5% after U.S. and Iran halt attacks
byline: Oil prices plunged by more than 5% in early Asian trade on Monday as the U.S. and Iran halted attacks after two weeks of escalation that had driven Brent above $100.

title: Fresh controversy over Colombo national school's dry ration drive
byline: Fresh controversy has erupted over the disputed dry ration collection drive at Thurstan College after the school’s parents’ union alleged that some of the donated food items had already expired and claimed the distribution programme had been shifted from Delft Island (Neduntheevu) to schools in Jaffna following media scrutiny.

title: Sri Lankan faces backlash over ‘ego-driven’ expansion plans, soaring maintenance costs and CEO vacuum
byline: SriLankan Airlines’ new Chairman Dimal Arandara is drawing heavy scrutiny over an unconventional strategic proposal to balance the national carrier’s bloated staff-to-aircraft ratio by purchasing more aircraft instead of right-sizing the workforce.

title: Legal experts flag unique compliance landscape in staggered PDPA rollout
byline: The enforcement of Sri Lanka’s Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA) No. 9 of 2022 has taken a definitive step forward with a recent gazette notification declaring January 1, 2027, as the operational date for several key sections.

title: Rupee weakens slightly against US Dollar
byline: The Sri Lankan Rupee depreciated slightly against the US Dollar today (27), according to the latest exchange rates released by the Central Bank of Sri Lanka.

title: Horana tuition centre owner arrested with crystal meth
byline: The owner of a private tuition centre in Horana has been arrested for allegedly possessing the narcotic drug known as ’’Ice’’ (crystal methamphetamine), police said.

title: Former State Minister Shantha Bandara’s son granted bail
byline: Five suspects, including Anuda Janadith Bandara, the son of former State Minister Shantha Bandara, have been granted bail by the Fort Magistrate’s Court in connection with the alleged robbery of Rs. 20 million belonging to a Chinese national.

title: Very happy if BASL issues statement on Wijeyadasa or his son: Chathuranga
byline: Deputy Minister Chathuranga Abeysinghe said he would be ’’very happy’’ to see the Bar Association of Sri Lanka (BASL) issue a statement regarding former Justice Minister Wijeyadasa Rajapakshe or his son, questioning whether the association applies the same standards in all cases.

title: Shooting at U.S. Seattle food festival leaves 2 dead, wounds 5
byline: Two people were killed, and five others were wounded in a shooting on Sunday (July 26, 2026) evening during a food festival at an events complex near the Space Needle in Seattle, a city fire department spokesperson said.

title: Three-wheeler driver killed in Gothatuwa road accident
byline: A three-wheeler driver was killed in a road accident in the Gothatuwa area this morning (27), Police said.

title: AI will take away SL’s business outsourcing revenue: MP
byline: Indicating that artificial intelligence (AI) will affect Sri Lanka’s economy in an unimaginable way, Opposition MP Ravi Karunanayake said it has already begun to take away the revenue which the country has been generating out of business process outsourcing.

title: Sri Lanka, India review progress of key development projects
byline: Minister of Labour and Deputy Minister of Finance and Planning Dr. Anil Jayantha Fernando today held discussions with Indian High Commissioner to Sri Lanka Santosh Jha to review the progress of development projects being implemented with financial assistance from the Government of India.

title: Iran says no talks underway with US, sets conditions for future negotiations
byline: Iran said Monday that it is not currently engaged in negotiations with the US and that any future talks would depend on Washington changing its conduct.

title: Bodies of five climbers found on Russia’s highest mountain
byline: Russia says it has found the bodies of five foreign climbers – believed to be Bosnian – on Mount Elbrus, authorities and state media say.

title: US, Sri Lanka launch CARAT 2026 maritime exercise
byline: The United States and Sri Lanka have launched the sixth edition of the Cooperation Afloat Readiness and Training (CARAT) exercise, a bilateral maritime program aimed at strengthening cooperation in maritime security, humanitarian assistance, disaster response, and regional readiness.

title: Strong winds forecast over several areas; public urged to take precautions
byline: The Department of Meteorology has issued a warning of strong winds over several parts of the country and the surrounding sea areas due to active southwest monsoon conditions.

title: Colombo University signs MoU with Sri Lanka Inventors Commission to boost innovation
byline: The University of Colombo has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Sri Lanka Inventors Commission (SLIC) to strengthen innovation, entrepreneurship, and the commercialization of research.

title: Rs. 200,000 paid to shoot Dehiwala Cemetery guard; Gunman arrested
byline: Police have arrested the alleged gunman involved in the shooting of a security guard at the Nisala Sewana public cemetery in Dehiwala-Mount Lavinia, Deputy Inspector General (DIG) of Police for the Colombo District, Nishantha de Zoysa, said today (27).

title: Wildlife Department gets new vehicles to tackle elephant conflicts
byline: The Department of Wildlife Conservation (DWC) has launched a programme to strengthen field operations and improve efforts to mitigate human-elephant conflicts by providing new vehicles, including double cabs and motorcycles, to its officers.

title: Cabinet approves proposal to extend judges’ retirement age by two years
byline: The Cabinet has approved a controversial proposal to extend the retirement age of judges by two years.

title: President discusses issues in developing cricket in Sri Lanka
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake held a meeting with the Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC)

title: Kavadi dances allowed at Devinuwara Perahera despite earlier police concerns
byline: Public Security Minister Ananda Wijepala has granted permission for all 45 Kavadi dance troupes that participated in last year’s procession to take part in this year’s Devinuwara Esala Perahera.

title: South Korea court gives ex-President Yoon suspended jail term for violating election law
byline: A South Korean court on Monday sentenced former President Yoon Suk Yeol to 18 months in prison, suspended for ​three years, after finding him guilty of violating the election law ‌by making false statements during his 2022 presidential campaign.

title: Concerns raised over delayed Colombo Port crane removal tender
byline: The tender to remove four old gantry cranes from the Colombo Port’s Jaya Container Terminal has been delayed for the third time, causing concerns among several bidders.
